# Viruses and the host

> *Viral disease comes from the death of infected cells, from the immune response that removes them, and from viruses that persist for life.*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
The plan for this chapter:
:::

| Part of the chapter | Plan |
|---|---|
| Learning objectives | Relate tropism to receptors; place viral damage on the damage-response framework; distinguish acute, latent and chronic viral infection |
| Tropism and spread in the body | Receptors, entry sites, spread by blood and nerves |
| Patterns of damage | Cytopathic effect; immune-mediated damage; transformation and cancer; a table of mechanisms with anchor examples |
| Persistence | Latency and reactivation (herpesviruses), chronic infection (HIV); a spectrum from acute to lifelong |
| Interferons and immunity | Brief link to the immunology course |
| Scenario questions | Which host factor or pattern best explains a presentation |
